claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr in practice contains crystallographic defects.
Available thermal-conductivity measurements include HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing about 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed explainable ML approach incorporates defect and oxygen data from related binary-alloy and high-entropy-alloy systems.
The ML approach will predict HfNbTaTiZr thermal conductivity more accurately than standard analytical models in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes.
Standard analytical thermal-conductivity models for this problem assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Defects in HfNbTaTiZr scatter heat carriers.
Oxygen contamination modifies the electronic structure of HfNbTaTiZr.
Defect scattering and oxygen-induced electronic-structure changes alter phonon and electron transport.
Learning defect and oxygen effects from prior binary-alloy and HEA datasets allows the model to adjust electron and lattice-related scattering contributions.
Accounting for defects and oxygen will overcome an accuracy limitation caused by perfect-lattice assumptions.
The ML predictions will match measured thermal conductivity more closely across both temperature regimes.
Oxygen-contaminated HfNbTaTiZr specimens exhibit discrepancies that the ML model can particularly resolve.
Neglecting defect scattering and oxygen effects makes existing analytical conductivity predictions less accurate.
Oxygen contamination is a relevant research variable in refractory complex concentrated alloys and refractory high-entropy alloys.
The approach is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with oxygen levels near 1 wt.% and temperatures in 0–200 K or 300–1200 K.
Applicability to other alloys or substantially different oxygen levels is uncertain.
The magnitude of the accuracy improvement depends on the quality and relevance of the transferred training data.
Predicted alloy properties can be tested experimentally.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant reduction in conductivity-prediction error relative to analytical models across both regimes would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and conditions appear to cover both ordinarily defective samples and samples containing 1 wt.% oxygen, while the boundary states that the approach is valid only for material with oxygen contamination near 1 wt.%, leaving the oxygen-free or differently contaminated portion of the stated scope inconsistent.
